quotes.text: This reader is compatible with JavaScript SDK, iOS SDK, Android SDK, React Native SDK, and server-driven integrations.
Failing to install a required update can prevent a reader from accepting payments.
The actual battery life varies depending on product settings and deployed features.

findings: The complete November hardware reference retains the Android smart reader, countertop and handheld use, customizable UI, internet/LAN/handoff connectivity and four SDK platforms plus server-driven. Server-driven is recommended for separate-device POS when offline card collection is not needed.

Stripe maintains four software components: reader application, firmware, configuration and key identifier. Updates are automatic when the reader is idle. Leave it on and powered for assigned-location midnight updates. The daily PCI reboot and morning POS disconnect are documented, and a reboot manually checks for updates. Required updates may block payment acceptance. A failed Stripe connectivity diagnostic blocks processing and updates in the guide's connectivity troubleshooting context.

Both snapshots keep the liquid-ingress handling, LED-state meanings, 12W recommended power, USB-A warning, up to 30 minutes to recover a deeply discharged battery with its display off, reduced charging outside 15–45°C, and charging stopped below 0°C or above 60°C. The captures omit LED icons/colors, so use the text as a list of meanings without assigning appearance.
substantive_changes: The November 7 regional software table lists reader 2.46.4.0, firmware 1.00.08.01 and ROM 2.2.24.1002 for all its rows, compared with May 1 reader 2.41.2.0, firmware 1.00.03.00 and ROM 2.2.22. It adds MX, HK and the BG/HR/CY/EE/HU/LV/LI/LT/MT/RO/SK/SI regional configuration row.

Reader application releases are added through October 20, 2026. September 8 reader 2.45.7.0 specifically fixes clipping of long translated tip text and occasional countertop-mode auto-disconnects. The firmware changelog gains four entries through 1.00.07.00.

The November page integrates a hardware specifications table with battery capacity and estimated times, USB-C or accessory dock, Wi-Fi plus optional Ethernet hub, S710-only 4G/LTE, Android 10 and the stated camera, microphone and security scope. This documents hardware distinctions in this page and does not imply a hardware rollout.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May 1 regional software table and April 20 changelog entry dated, plus the older separate software-acceptance bundle release-note route from May. The prior raw filename's 2025 suffix does not set its fetched date.

Preserve dated NFC UID support via Terminal.collectData in firmware 1.00.00.25 and the pre-insert card changelog's version 2.28 and Stripe-controlled feature flag. The 50% battery entry is specifically for a configuration or key update on battery.
Retain app version, firmware version, ROM and configuration as separate values. The listed PCI identifier mapping and day-to-day update/diagnostic behavior are present in both captures.
conflicts: The current summary's 'All 5 SDKs + server-driven' overcounts the four named SDKs. Server-driven is the fifth listed integration path.

November's table lists 1.00.08.01, while its firmware release-history table ends at 1.00.07.00 dated September 8. Report the two separately. The October 20 entry 2.46.4.0 is reader application history and does not supply a firmware date.

The separate setup route tracks individual model availability. A combined S700/S710 regional software row for Mexico, Hong Kong or the added country group does not establish that both models or S710 cellular service are available throughout that group.

Both captures name reader application, firmware, configuration and key identifier as software components (old raw line 101; new raw line 102). Keep ROM separate from the key identifier; these tables disclose no per-row key identifiers.
unresolved_questions: The 1.00.08.01 firmware release date/history entry is absent from the November changelog, and regional software rows do not identify per-model or per-account availability.
The May software-acceptance pointer is omitted from November. The compared pages do not establish retirement or a changed fleet acceptance procedure.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-reader-s700-s710, source-stripe-terminal-s700-s710 summarizes an Android smart reader for countertop or handheld use, with internet/LAN/handoff and customizable UI. The November and May captures list JavaScript, iOS, Android and React Native SDKs plus server-driven. Stripe recommends server-driven when the POS is on a separate device and offline card collection is unnecessary (old raw lines 11-17, new raw lines 12-18). The merchant can run reader diagnostics for DNS, Stripe and Terminal-event connectivity, Wi-Fi and hardware. In connectivity troubleshooting, Stripe says the Stripe connectivity test must pass for processing and updates. Deeply discharged units can show an LED while the display stays dark during up to 30 minutes of slow charge. The merchant should supply the recommended 12W using the supplied adapter or suitable USB-C, with a USB-A warning (old raw lines 48-77, new raw lines 49-78). Stripe supplies automatic idle updates. Leaving the device powered allows assigned-location midnight updates, and the reader restarts daily for PCI and disconnects from the POS app. Rebooting can check manually, and missing a required update can prevent accepting payments (old raw lines 93-105, new raw lines 94-106). The mapped summary's April latest label is historical, and its SDK count is inaccurate. The November table now lists reader 2.46.4.0, firmware 1.00.08.01 and ROM 2.2.24.1002, and its hardware table reports S710-only 4G/LTE and estimated battery life (old raw lines 107-121, old raw lines 359-364, new raw lines 108-125, new raw lines 386-407).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-reader-s700-s710, source-stripe-terminal-s700-s710 needs a dated source update. May 1 reported 2.41.2.0 / 1.00.03.00 / ROM 2.2.22 and included a separate software-acceptance bundle release-note pointer. November 7 lists 2.46.4.0 / 1.00.08.01 / ROM 2.2.24.1002, adds MX, HK and BG/HR/CY/EE/HU/LV/LI/LT/MT/RO/SK/SI configurations, and its firmware history stops at 1.00.07.00. The October 20 reader application entry and September 8 translated-tip and countertop auto-disconnect fixes deserve explicit dated attribution, without assigning an unsupported firmware release date (old raw lines 107-123, old raw lines 333-339, new raw lines 108-145, new raw lines 357-367). Both captures describe four software components: reader application, firmware, configuration and key identifier (old raw line 101; new raw line 102). Their regional tables give Reader, Firmware, Configuration and ROM; no per-row key identifier is disclosed, and ROM is a separate value (old raw lines 107-115; new raw lines 108-119). The device specs are substantive documentary additions. They give 140 hours standby and 15 hours active as estimates dependent on settings and deployed features. They list front and rear cameras and microphones physically present but unsupported, the audio jack as supported, and 4G/LTE on S710 only (new raw lines 386-396, new raw lines 399-407). The revised battery-link anchor and image asset are navigation/presentation, just as changed table spacing, numbering and punctuation leave existing guidance intact (old raw line 9, old raw lines 19-31, old raw lines 359-364, new raw line 10, new raw lines 20-32, new raw lines 386-415). Keep the Terminal concept's reciprocal source link, plus the separate model setup and accessories routes. Regional software rows alone do not establish either model's country rollout, and the omitted May fleet pointer does not establish retirement. Preserve the dated pre-insert feature flag and historical NFC UID support (old raw lines 192-196, old raw line 344, new raw lines 216-220, new raw line 372).
